deliverables.text: A coordinate-plane sketch of the bracket's four vertices showing The Straight Run layout built by translating the bracket twice down the sheet, labeling each translated copy's new vertex coordinates.

Reflect the bracket across the x-axis and translate the reflected copy by the stated kerf spacing to build The Mirror Cut's interlocking pair; give the new coordinates, identify the line of symmetry of the interlocked pair, and verify with coordinates that the pair is symmetric about that line.
Rotate the original bracket 180 degrees about the D2 midpoint and show it produces the identical interlocked outline that D2's reflection-then-translation produced.

Rotate the two-part interlocked block's bounding-box corners 90 degrees counterclockwise about the origin and give the new bounding box's dimensions, to check the block fits the laser bed either way it is loaded.

Find the scale factor of the dilation mapping the full-size bracket to the shop's existing QC gauge, then use a stated new scale factor to dilate the bracket's coordinates and find a second gauge's vertices.
Full nesting takeoff: brackets per sheet, material cost per bracket, and machine-time cost per bracket for each layout, combined into net cost per finished bracket; state the winner and margin.

balance.argument_a: The Mirror Cut yields 219 brackets per sheet (12% better than The Straight Run's 196, per the sourced real-world mirrored-nesting yield improvement) at a material cost of $1.31454/bracket -- 10.5% cheaper on material alone than The Straight Run's $1.4688/bracket. Even after Appendix E's MA1/MA2 add real machine-time cost for the slower, more-pierced mirrored toolpath ($0.01770/bracket vs. $0.01139/bracket), The Mirror Cut still wins on the graded net-cost-per-bracket metric, $1.33224 vs. $1.48019 -- a 9.99% win, not the full 10.5% material-only win, showing the machine-time cost is real but does not erase the material advantage.
balance.argument_b: The Straight Run needs zero of Appendix E's stated assumptions to defend its number -- every bracket gets one pierce and the sourced full cutting speed, with no estimate standing between the appendix data and the $1.48019/bracket figure. The Mirror Cut's better number depends on three separate stated assumptions (MA1 pierce count, MA2 speed penalty, and MA3's reject rate revealed by the twist) all pointing the same direction; if a shop's real mirrored toolpath runs closer to Appendix E's more severe flex values, or if the customer's inspection tolerance is stricter than assumed, The Straight Run's plain, assumption-free number is the safer one to build a fixed three-year quote on.
balance.margin_basis: Net cost per finished bracket (material cost + machine-time cost) for each layout, computed in cases/the-mirror-cut/sensitivity_model.py, evaluate(PARAMS), from Appendix A/B/C/D figures.

derived._note: Computed by cases/the-mirror-cut/sensitivity_model.py, evaluate(PARAMS)/evaluate_twist(PARAMS). case-readiness should re-derive independently.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Pierces per bracket, The Mirror Cut, as a multiple of The Straight Run's one pierce per bracket
modeling_assumptions.basis: Tightly interlocked, mirrored nests are commonly pre-pierced ahead of full contour cutting to manage heat buildup between closely spaced parts, rather than cut as one continuous pass -- a real, documented nesting practice (S8). No public per-shop study times this exact multiplier for this exact part geometry; the 2x figure is the case author's own estimate from how the operation is actually sequenced.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Not enough on its own to flip the primary metric -- material cost dominates the per-bracket total. Flexed +/-50% in Tier 2 probe 5.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Cutting speed, The Mirror Cut, as a fraction of The Straight Run's sourced cutting speed
modeling_assumptions.basis: Closely nested, alternating-orientation parts require the machine to sequence and pace cuts so heat has room to dissipate between adjacent brackets rather than building up and warping them -- a real, documented general phenomenon in laser nesting (S8). No public per-shop study measures this exact slowdown for this exact geometry; 70% is the case author's own estimate.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Same as MA1 -- moves the machine-time line but does not by itself flip the primary metric. Flexed +/-50% in Tier 2 probe 5.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Rejected-part rate from heat-affected-zone distortion, each layout
modeling_assumptions.value_used: The Straight Run: 1%. The Mirror Cut: 4%.
modeling_assumptions.basis: Heat-affected-zone buildup between closely nested, alternating-orientation parts is a real, documented distortion risk (S8); The Mirror Cut's tighter spacing carries more of that risk than The Straight Run's more open layout. No public per-shop reject-rate study exists for this exact part and nest, so both values are the case author's own estimate.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: The answer is sensitive to this value -- see FACILITATOR.md and case.json's balance object.

sensitivity_note: The graded primary metric (net cost per finished bracket) already includes machine-time cost (MA1/MA2), and remains stable under a +/-50% flex of either assumption -- The Mirror Cut wins by roughly 9-10% across the flex range. MA3's reject-rate assumption is not part of the graded metric at all; it is revealed only by the Twist, where it narrows (but per the base case's flex range, does not reverse) The Mirror Cut's advantage.
